clue.text: Something in the garden for pet owl to chew

indicators.note: what is chewed gets mangled and broken up, so the letters before it are mashed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, though it reads like a joining word

explanation.surface: A gardener sets out something for a pet owl to peck and chew on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' does double duty in the surface but its letters belong to the fodder: FOR plus PET OWL rearranges to FLOWERPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowerpot is a container for plants, an ordinary item found around a garden.

clue.text: Undeserving rich and their pampered pets?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wealthy, privileged people thought to be overpaid
second meaning, taken literally: overfed household cats

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading: the pets of the rich would be well-fed felines.
explanation.definitionFit: Fat cats is an idiom for wealthy, overpaid bosses, and literally describes plump, spoilt felines.

clue.text: Eloquent preacher's year in church

parts.note: an orator is a skilled public speaker
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A fine preacher spends a year giving sermons in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratory is a small chapel or place of prayer, so a kind of church.

clue.text: Nymph has bedroom that creates sound effects

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'a room that creates sound effects'

parts.note: Echo is the nymph of Greek myth who could only repeat others' words
a chamber is an old word for a bedroom

explanation.surface: A mythical nymph owns a bedroom with odd acoustics.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo chamber is an enclosure with reverberant walls used to produce echo effects in recordings.

clue.text: Could this suggest daughter only nine? Imagine!

parts.note: someone only nine is 'pre-ten', not yet ten years old
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent marvels that their daughter is only nine.
explanation.walkthrough: The playful idea is that a girl of nine is a 'pre-ten D', a daughter before ten; read together the letters make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend is to make believe, the same as to imagine something is so.

clue.text: Best, perhaps, granny's hairpiece

parts.note: top means best, as in 'top quality'
a granny is a type of knot, and 'perhaps' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: Grandma's hair arranged in her best style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'granny' looks like an old lady but is the granny knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a tuft or bun of hair worn on top of the head, a hair arrangement or ornament.

clue.text: Extremely plaintive, desperate appeal for money abroad

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the two end letters of the word that follows

parts.note: its first and last letters
SOS is the distress signal

explanation.surface: A mournful, frantic plea for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The peso is the currency of Mexico and several other countries, so foreign money.

clue.text: Foreign character turns up in Paris park

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: found across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A foreigner shows up in a park in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Psi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and 'character' in crosswords often means a letter.

clue.text: Put off seeing how library books are displayed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: postponed or set aside

definitions.text: seeing how library books are displayed?

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second meaning is a literal description rather than a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that is shelved is postponed; books that are shelved have been put on shelves.

clue.text: Unusual way to the mountains

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
a range is a line of mountains

explanation.surface: An odd route that leads up to the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange and unusual are synonyms, both meaning out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Time for everyone to pass on their knowledge

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
each, every one

explanation.surface: It's time for all to share what they know.
explanation.definitionFit: To teach is to instruct others, handing on what one has learned.

clue.text: New to drink, run empire badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the preceding letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newcomer starts drinking and runs an empire into the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New to drink' reads like a novice drinker, but it defines wine sold young.
explanation.definitionFit: En primeur is the French wine-trade term for buying wine while it is still in the barrel, before release.

clue.text: Notice love is a great bother

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Discovering that love is a lot of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb, to observe, but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or trouble, as in 'much ado about nothing'.

clue.text: Having nothing to face?

parts.note: surface reading: having no troubles or challenges to confront
setter's reading: nothing growing on one's face, no beard or stubble

explanation.walkthrough: 'face' as a verb suggests a problem to confront; read as the noun it means no hair on the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose whiskers are all removed has a bare chin and cheeks.

clue.text: S for Sovereign

definitions.meaning: first meaning, cryptic: the letter S starts the word 'state', so it is its head
second meaning: a monarch, who leads a nation

explanation.surface: S as the abbreviation of Sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like an abbreviation glossary; in fact S is literally the leading letter of 'state'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign is the ruling monarch, the top figure of a nation.

clue.text: Died after aerial battle: going to heaven?

indicators.note: after says the single word before it is placed behind the phrase that follows

parts.note: sky, the aerial domain
a war is a battle
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A pilot killed in a dogfight goes up to heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks 'heaven' as the sky rather than the afterlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Skyward means upward toward the sky, playfully the heavens.

clue.text: Two shortly become confused in silly talk

indicators.note: shortly asks for the word to be cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
to addle is to muddle

explanation.surface: A pair soon get muddled during a foolish conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is nonsense, foolish or trivial chatter.

clue.text: Hotel room may have this ban on short skirt

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, so the first word goes after

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A hotel forbids guests from wearing miniskirts.
explanation.definitionFit: A minibar is a small fridge of drinks provided in a hotel bedroom.

clue.text: Scotsman, the first person that's regularly driven over

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'what is regularly driven over'

parts.note: Mac, from the Gaelic 'son of', is a familiar name for a Scot
Adam is the first man in the Bible

explanation.surface: A Scot is the first person ever to be run over by a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Macadam is the crushed-stone road surface invented by John McAdam, which vehicles drive on.

clue.text: Arsenal supporter heading off into New York women's house

indicators.note: into tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York

indicators.note: heading off means the front letter is lost

parts.note: Arsenal Football Club are nicknamed the Gunners

explanation.surface: An Arsenal fan heads off to a women's refuge in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a north London football club whose fans and players are called Gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: A nunnery is a convent, a residence for a community of nuns.

clue.text: Something done on the brass perhaps, causing some friction

definitions.text: Something done on the brass perhaps
definitions.meaning: first meaning: an impression taken of an engraved church brass
second meaning: chafing one surface against another

explanation.walkthrough: 'the brass' hints at senior officers or money, but means a memorial plate copied with paper and wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass rubbing copies a monumental brass; rubbing also means creating friction by contact.

clue.text: Showing arrogance, paid sportsman perhaps duly sacked

parts.note: a professional athlete, paid to play

indicators.note: a sacked town is ransacked and left in disorder, so these letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A haughty professional athlete is fired, as he deserved.
explanation.definitionFit: To act proudly is to behave with conceit or haughtiness.

clue.text: Perhaps dog at college a bloomer

parts.note: a dog is an example of a pet
uni is short for university
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog brought to college makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A petunia is a garden flower, so something that blooms.

clue.text: Certificate Foreign Office employee doesn't complete

indicators.note: something not completed falls short of its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a diplomat works for the Foreign Office

explanation.surface: A Foreign Office worker never finishes the course that earns a certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Foreign Office is the UK government department for foreign affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is a document awarded on completing a course of study.

clue.text: Told a tale about drug being craved

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to yarn is to tell a long story
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone recounted a story about a drug they had been longing for.
explanation.definitionFit: To have yearned is to have longed for something intensely.

clue.text: Adds something against eulogies

parts.note: con, as in pros and cons, means against
eulogies are tributes of praise

explanation.surface: Someone chips in an objection to a set of speeches praising the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To contribute is to give or supply something toward a whole.

clue.text: Tiny vegetable, and not a whole fruit

indicators.note: not whole means incomplete, so the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A small vegetable and part of a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea is a small round green seed eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Newly initiated into food authority

indicators.note: newly suggests a fresh version, so the word after it is remade with its letters reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recent recruit admitted into a body governing food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like a container signal but is only a link: all nine letters of 'initiated' rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A dietitian is a professional expert on nutrition and diet.

clue.text: Man a terrible tsar? Not very

indicators.note: not tells us the abbreviation that follows must be left out

parts.note: Ivan the Terrible was a sixteenth-century tsar of Russia
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Was this man a dreadful tsar? Not really.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian is a male first name, and 'man' in crosswords often stands for a man's name.

clue.text: A hard growth seen on oak

definitions.text: A hard growth seen on oak

parts.note: taken as written
a corn is a patch of hardened skin on the foot

explanation.surface: A tough knob found growing on an oak tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer while its first words also build it.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the hard-shelled nut that develops on oak trees.

clue.text: PM meeting an indigenous American

parts.note: Theresa May was UK Prime Minister
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister meets a Native American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' could be afternoon, but here it is a British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maya are an indigenous people of Central America, and Mayan describes one of them.

clue.text: It may be close to the church, or a serious distance

definitions.text: It may be close to the church

parts.note: grave means serious
a yard is a unit of distance

explanation.surface: Something could lie near the church, or a long way off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' suggests nearness, though a burial ground may sit in a church's close or precinct.
explanation.definitionFit: A graveyard is a burial ground, typically beside a church.
